## portcheck servers

List the dev servers you started, with their project and uptime

### Synopsis

List your own processes that listen on a TCP port and run inside a project
folder, oldest first: dev servers, databases and tools you started from a
terminal or editor and may have forgotten about.

The project is the nearest folder at or above the process's working
directory that holds .git, package.json, go.mod or a similar file. Apps that
run from / or your home folder (AirPlay, Spotify, …) are left out unless you
pass --all.

With --stop, the listed servers are stopped after confirmation, with the same
safety guards as 'portcheck kill'.

```
portcheck servers [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  portcheck servers
  portcheck servers --older-than 1d
  portcheck servers --older-than 12h --stop
  portcheck servers --all --json
```

### Options

```
      --all                 also include your processes that run outside a project folder
      --dry-run             with --stop: show what would be stopped
      --grace duration      with --stop: how long to wait for a graceful exit (default 5s)
  -h, --help                help for servers
      --older-than string   only servers running at least this long, e.g. 30m, 12h, 2d
      --stop                stop the listed servers (asks first)
  -y, --yes                 with --stop: do not ask for confirmation
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --json                shorthand for --output json
      --log-format string   log format: text or json (default "text")
      --no-color            disable colors (also honors NO_COLOR)
  -o, --output string       output format: table, plain, csv, json (default: table on a terminal, plain otherwise)
  -v, --verbose             log diagnostic details to stderr
```
